title: fix(validate-commit): Update the regexp
body:
The current regexp was sometime refusing commit messages that are
valid (see
https://travis-ci.org/algolia/instantsearch.js/builds/85530333)

I've simply removed the `?:` and added a check on the `:`, and this
seems to work better.

I still have no idea why some commits where ok and some not. If anyone
has a guess...?

comments.body:
Wait there's something we do not understand here, the current regex is fine: https://regex101.com/r/kC6sQ8/1

And on you other PR #252 its completely OK. @redox can you help?

> I've simply removed the ?: and added a check on the :, and this
> seems to work better.

Hmmm, I don't see why it would be better :/ The `?:` is just to make a non-capturing group :/

This is really weird.

```
echo 'perf(a): test' | grep -qE '^(?:feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|revert)\(.+\).*' # OK
echo 'feat(a): test' | grep -qE '^(?:feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|revert)\(.+\).*' # KO
```
My bad sorry, non capturing groups are not part of POSIX (grep): https://lists.debian.org/debian-live/2012/05/msg00022.html

Seems like the first element of the `|` list does not work. If I remove the `?:` it works.

So basically, it should fail on every `feat()`, still some PR are passing

> This is really weird.
> 
> echo 'perf(a): test' | grep -qE '^(?:feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|revert)(.+)._' # OK
> echo 'feat(a): test' | grep -qE '^(?:feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|revert)(.+)._' # KO

Ahaha, I was testing it on my Mac and the `grep` there is happy with non-capturing group :)
